verdict.rationale: Google Workspace's own Context-Aware Access lets admins create app access policies that use device security status, and endpoint management covers managed endpoints. Community reports confirm these policies block access from non-compliant setups, such as browsers without the Endpoint Verification plugin, though full enforcement depends on Chrome and Endpoint Verification. missing for 10: explicit documentation that encryption, screen-lock and managed-state attributes can be used as policy conditions, evidence that posture is evaluated before the app session is granted, and full device-verification enforcement outside Chrome.

support.subject: As a security engineer, only healthy devices get in — device posture (managed, encrypted, screen-locked) is checked in the auth policy before an app session is granted

citations.quote: you can create granular access control security policies for apps based on attributes, such as user identity, location, device security status, and IP address
With Google endpoint management, you can make your organization's data more secure across your users' mobile devices, desktops, laptops, and other endpoints.
User speculated a login block was 'a Context-Aware Access thing' since 'Firefox doesn't support Endpoint Verification plugin'
